2608.26083.title: ICON Decomposition: Multivariate Concept-Level Explanations of Deep Representations for Model Auditing
2608.26083.paper_summary: Deep neural networks often exploit spurious associations in their training data, a failure known as shortcut learning. Concept-based explainability methods screen for shortcuts by testing whether concepts such as a patient's sex or scanner settings can be decoded from a network layer. Because each concept is evaluated in isolation, these methods can mistake correlations between concepts as evidence that the model uses them. We introduce ICON decomposition, which instead quantifies how much of a layer's variance each concept explains after accounting for all other concepts and the outcome. On synthetic data with known ground truth, ICON recovers concept importance more accurately than seven alternative baseline methods. On skin-lesion and brain-imaging models, it isolates the concepts on which a model genuinely relies, quantifies the representation unexplained by any of the supplied concepts, and yields sparse explanations that we validate by retraining and out-of-distribution testing.
2608.26083.paper_summary_zh: 深度神經網絡經常利用訓練數據中的虛假關聯，這種失敗稱為捷徑學習。基於概念的可解釋性方法通過測試像患者性別或掃描儀設置等概念是否可以從網絡層解碼來篩選捷徑。由於每個概念都是孤立評估的，這些方法可能會將概念之間的相關性誤認為模型使用它們的證據。我們引入了ICON分解，該方法量化了在考慮所有其他概念和結果後，每個概念解釋層變異性的程度。在具有已知真實值的合成數據上，ICON比七種替代基準方法更準確地恢復概念重要性。在皮膚病變和腦成像模型上，它隔離了模型真正依賴的概念，量化了任何提供的概念無法解釋的表示，並產生稀疏的解釋，我們通過重新訓練和分佈外測試來驗證這些解釋。
